messages:
jamie ong: DeployBot flagged a spike in 5xxs for embeddings after v2.14.0 canary in ap-southeast1. Suggesting auto-rollback to v2.13.9.
deploy-bot: DeployBot: Canary failure detected for release v2.14.0. error-rate on /v1/embeddings = 3.8% (threshold 1%). Recommended action: auto-rollback to v2.13.9. reason: kv-cache-corruption-detect
lee chen: Hold the auto-rollback. The change touched KV cache serialization; rolling back the binary without reversing cache format will leave live caches incompatible and cause more 5xxs.
maria ortiz: +1. We have >100k cache entries generated during canary that assume new serialization. Rolling back risks invalidating them and creating a bigger outage.
jamie ong: Ops options: A) Manual rollback and run cache warmers + migrate caches back (risky) B) Keep v2.14.0, isolate affected customer pool, deploy a one-line hotfix to accept both serialization formats and drain older caches gracefully C) Pin new customers to older version while we hotfix. Thoughts?
lee chen: B looks safest: deploy a compatibility shim that tries new deserialize, falls back to old in case of error. That way we avoid global rollback and cache-flush storms. We can stage fix as v2.14.0-hotfix and route 10% test-slice first.
maria ortiz: How fast can we get shim out? Needs review but it's a tiny change. I can produce artifact in ~8m. If hotfix fails within 12m, we'll proceed with staged rollback + careful cache migration.
ops-bot: Note: DeployBot will auto-rollback in 5m unless overridden by operator. Use DeployBot override to prevent auto-rollback.
jamie ong: @deploy-bot please hold auto-rollback, operator override incoming. Ops will prepare route pin commands in parallel.
lee chen: Route pin example (ops):
```bash
routectl set-weight --route dedicated-ap-southeast1 --version v2.13.9 --weight 100 --match-label "customer_type: legacy-pool"
```
maria ortiz: Hotfix build done: v2.14.0-shim (includes dual-deserialize fallback). Running canary on 5% test-slice now.
maria ortiz: Canary result: test-slice error-rate 0.4% (good). Also verified existing cached items deserialize with fallback.
deploy-bot: DeployBot: Canary metrics improved for v2.14.0-shim on test-slice. Auto-rollback cancelled by operator override.
jamie ong: Ops: run step to pin only newly onboarded dedicated customers to v2.13.9 for 30m while we monitor. That avoids touching long-running jobs.
lee chen: Pin executed, verified. Existing sessions remain on v2.14.0-shim. New enrollments routed to v2.13.9.
maria ortiz: Running gradual rollback plan prepped if needed: 1) drain v2.14.0 traffic to 0 in 5-minute windows 2) run cache-migration job to reserialize entries 3) restore traffic. This will be manual and announced if executed.
jamie ong: Customer-facing blurb (short): "We detected an embedding cache compatibility issue in ap-southeast1 after today's release. We deployed a compatibility hotfix and temporarily routed new customers to the previous stable release to protect in-flight workloads. We'll provide an update in 30 minutes with monitoring results." Keep it concise.
oncall-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2109, severity: P2, region: ap-southeast1 dedicated, mitigation: compatibility shim + routing pin; follow-up: postmortem and release-note addendum.
lee chen: Decision: no immediate global rollback. Actions: - maria: monitor hotfix + open PR for postmortem checks - ops: keep pin for 30m and be ready to execute manual rollback plan if errors spike - jamie: coordinate customer comms and update release notes. Closing when postmortem link is posted.
